verdict: Red 8/10 REJECT, blue 8/10 PARTIALLY OVERTURNED - but overturned on MECHANISM only; the verdict, the stance and the sizing are concordant, and blue independently supplied a stronger kill than the one it demolished. That is why this is a KILL and not an ESCALATE: both benches land on no long, no RP_FAIR, FLAT, with no conditional entry band and a genuinely high reopen bar. The triage caught something the screen could not: UAMY's Q2 print landed at 4:15pm ET on 2026-08-11, AFTER the pack's tape was struck, and it carried an FY26 revenue guidance cut from $125M to $60-75M. The pack's $6.58 was the pre-print regular-session close. So the screened dislocation was measured on a price that never saw a 48% guidance halving. The triage's own print-decisive reconstruction is the best piece of work in the record and deserves to be carried forward as a template: the $125M guide, reiterated at Q1 on 2026-05-14, was refutable BEFORE the print from arithmetic alone - H1 revenue of $14.7M against $125M required an 8.5x second-half step-up, while the Rotterdam antimony assessment had already fallen two consecutive months and Q1's own realized price of $19.92/lb was rolling over from $28.32/lb. No new information was needed to know the guide was unmeetable, only two published revenue lines and a public price index. The court's mandate was a single binary the triage framed precisely: the DLA order book prices at roughly a 3x premium to spot - $2.6M invoiced on about 82,000 lbs of the first two shipments implies about $31.71/lb against $13.70/lb realized commercially and roughly $10.50/lb spot - so if the $57.3M booked against a $245M master contract is FIXED-PRICE, H2 gross profit is largely insulated and the guide cut overstates the economic damage; if it is spot-indexed or repriceable, the H2 case is hollow. That term is disclosed in no press release and swings H2 gross profit by roughly $25M. Red claimed to resolve it against the bull using the earnings-call transcript: the CEO said the cut 'has all to do with pricing, has nothing to do with delivery times' and the CFO said it was 'driven almost entirely by lower realized antimony pricing', which red argued is arithmetically incompatible with a fixed-dollar $57.3M backlog inside a $60-75M full-year guide. Blue overturned both horns of that dichotomy, and the manner of the overturn is the finding worth keeping. First, red inverted the desk's own venue rule: the WRITTEN 8-K gives TWO reasons - the price decline AND 'a shift to the future in the timing of certain DLA antimony metal ingot deliveries' - directly contradicting the transcript quote red built its FATAL on. Primary document beats transcript; red preferred the transcript because it was the more quotable. Second, blue actually read the 10-Q - reaching it via the r.jina.ai proxy after SEC 403'd every other route - and Note 5 gives a THIRD answer neither bench had: 'Pricing is determined at the time each delivery order is placed based on prevailing market rates along with certain specific fees.' Fixed-at-award per order, market-struck. Not repriceable, which kills red's horn; not a $31.71 fixed book, which kills the thesis's horn. And then blue's decisive new finding, which is what actually settles the case: the 10-Q shows orders totalling approximately $12M as of 6/30, against $57.3M 'on our books today' as of 8/11 - so roughly $45M, about 80% of the backlog, was placed in July and August, STRUCK AT POST-COLLAPSE PREVAILING RATES PLUS FEES. The thesis extrapolated one early high strike across the entire book. The dollars are secure; the economics are not insulated. There is no hidden $25M of gross profit. What survives on both benches is a valuation and promotion case, not a solvency one - and it is sufficient. At $5.34 (8/13 close, up 7.44% on the day, so the tape has traded and bounced rather than being the unreacted print the triage described) the cap is about $799M on 149.67M shares; less $62.1M of cash and treasuries and a $46.7M Larvotto stake gives roughly $690M of EV against a $67.5M guide midpoint, about 10x sales, at a 7-16% gross margin with a roughly $28M annual operating-loss run-rate and stock comp at 37% of revenue. Headline net income of $0.1M exists only via a $6.8M unrealized mark on the Larvotto stake; the operating loss was $7.0M. Q2's realized ASP was $13.70/lb against a $13.34/lb cost - a $0.36/lb unit spread, 2.6% - so this is a price-taker converter whose toll spread compressed rather than held. Blue's ruling that this fails RP_FAIR is correct and the reasoning matters: carry is NEGATIVE (a $28M annual operating-loss run-rate), so there is no fairly-paid carry to own, and fairness is unverifiable at 10x sales. The promotion texture stands as a sizing cut on both benches - the CEO appeared on Fox News on 8/07 and Bloomberg TV on 8/10, the two business days before halving guidance on 8/11, with an 'AI technology in mining' release on 7/15 - though blue materially corrected red on insiders: the 6/17 Form 4 red cited as insider supply is a director PURCHASE (Marinelli, 12,500 shares at about $7.45), and the 89,004-share disposal was in March. The insider picture is mixed, not one-way.
reopen_gates: Per-shipment DLA 8-Ks (monthly cadence since 7/01) showing realized pricing at or above $25/lb on RAMPING pounds, AND new order awards whose implied $/lb puts the 'certain specific fees' at 2x spot or better. Blue sharpened this from red's version and both halves are required - realized price alone is satisfiable by shipping the small early high-struck orders.

Throughput evidence that the book is deliverable: $57.3M at the implied ~$31.71/lb is about 1.81M lbs, which is 4.2x Q2's entire 428,425 lbs sold, in under five months, on a Thompson Falls expansion that only becomes fully operational on all furnaces during Q3. Even at post-collapse strikes the pound count is the binding constraint and neither bench resolved it.

Rotterdam antimony assessment stabilizing or reversing - the toll spread is $0.36/lb (2.6%) at a $13.70 ASP against a $13.34 cost, so this is a price-taker whose entire economics are the second derivative of the index.
Operating loss run-rate falling materially below $28M/yr with stock comp below 37% of revenue. Until then carry is negative and RP_FAIR cannot bind at any multiple.

A subsequent-events note confirming the $12M-at-6/30 versus $57.3M-at-8/11 backlog timing split, which blue tagged PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED. It is the load-bearing element of the decisive finding.
Price near the $3.93 low WITH firm-fixed-price delivery orders at struck values above spot - red's own stated change-my-mind condition, and the only path that reopens a long.
